questions.question: PQ is a diameter of a circle and PS is a chord. If PQ is 82 cm and PS is 80 cm, the distance (in cm) of PS from the center of the circle is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Diameter of the circle, PQ = 82 cm

Chord of the circle, PS = 80 cm

**Formula Used:**

Using the right triangle property in a circle:

If a chord is perpendicular to the diameter, the formula to find the distance from the center to the chord is:

Distance = sqrt{r² - (c/2)²}

Where, r = radius of the circle, c = length of the chord

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aa51723373cea246f13776398f4259bdc700d6952ab1de400912bd1b031d9a8a.png] 

Radius, r = PQ / 2 = 82 / 2 = 41 cm

Half of the chord, c/2 = 80 / 2 = 40 cm

Distance from the center = sqrt{41² - 40²}

Distance = sqrt{1681 - 1600}

Distance = sqrt{81}

Distance = 9 cm

**The distance of PS from the center of the circle is 9 cm.**

questions.question: PQ is a chord of a circle. The tangent XR at point X on the circle intersects the extension of PQ at point R. Given that XR = 12 cm, PQ = x cm, and QR = (x - 2) cm, find the value of x.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

XR = 12 cm (the length of the tangent)

PQ = x cm (the length of the chord)

QR = x - 2 cm (the external part of the secant)

**Formula used:**

According to the Power of a Point Theorem:

XR² = PR times QR

Where PR = PQ + QR = (x + (x - 2)) = 2x - 2

Substitute into the formula:

**Calculations:**

12² = (2x - 2)(x - 2)

⇒ 144 = 2x(x - 2) - 2(x - 2)

⇒ 144 = 2x² - 4x - 2x + 4

⇒ 144 = 2x² - 6x + 4

Move everything to one side:

⇒ 2x² - 6x + 4 - 144 = 0

⇒ 2x² - 6x - 140 = 0

Simplify the equation by dividing through by 2:

⇒ x² - 3x - 70 = 0

**Factoring the quadratic equation:**

(x - 10)(x + 7) = 0

So, x = 10 or x = -7

**Conclusion:**

Since x represents the length of PQ, it must be positive, so we discard x = -7.

**∴ x = 10 cm**.

questions.question: Two circles of radii 18 cm and 12 cm intersect each other and the length of their common chord is 16 cm. Then what is the distance (in cm) between their centres?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The Radii of the two circles are 18 cm and 12 cm.

The length of their common chord is 16 cm.

**Concept used:**

A line that is drawn perpendicular to the chord from the center of a circle always bisects the chord.

H² = B² + P²

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/91913594aa8fb525717bcc6cc8c7bef2131e66d3cf8782429636be650191b2d3.png] 

At first join O, P and A 

Now, OBA is a right angle triangle and PBA is also a right angle triangle.

Length of AB = AC/2 = 16/2 = 8 cm.

Again, OB² = 18² – 8² = 260

⇒ OB = √260 = 2√65 

And BP² = 12² – 8² = 80

⇒ BP = 4√5

Now distance between their centres is OP = OB + BP

⇒ OP = 2√65 + 4√5

⇒ OP = 2√5(2 + √13)

**∴ Distance (in cm) between their centers is 2√5(2 + √13)**

questions.question: AB is a chord of a circle with centre O, while PAQ is the tangent at A.R is a point on the minor arc AB. If ∠BAQ = 70°, then find the measure of ∠ARB .
questions.solution:
**Given:**

BAQ = 70º

PAQ is tangent at A

**Concept:**

The angle subtended by an arc at the center is double than subtended by it on other parts of the circle. In the figure below, ∠ AOB = 2 ∠ACB

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2749b2e6ee1edc094d103b0a4f3afd82cfa28175f96a6495f28e277eb63f62e4.png] 

**Calculations:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1f32f1a8032c9413751a0ca03582e97796af99b198defc2ec3820d1119a605cf.png] 

PAQ is tangent at point A i.e., ∠OAQ = 90º

From the figure, ∠OAB = ∠OAQ – ∠BAQ

⇒ ∠OAB = 90º – 70º = 20º

∠OBA = ∠OAB = 20º (since angle subtended by radius are equal)

In Δ OBA, ∠BOA = 180º – (∠OBA + ∠OAB)

⇒ ∠BOA = 180º – (20º + 20º) = 180º - 40º = 140º

∠BOA (exterior angle) = 360º – 140º = 220º

∠ARB = 1over 2∠BOA (exterior angle)

∠ARB = 1over 2 × (220º) = 110º

**The value of ∠ARB is 110º.**

questions.question: The vertices of a Δ ABC lie on a circle with centre O. AO is produced to meet the circle at the point P. D is a point on BC such that AD ⊥ BC. If ∠B = 68° and ∠C = 52°, then the measure of ∠DAP is:

AD ⊥ BC

∠B = 68° 

∠C = 52° 

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5095d80f27201a31a5dab09d3c67a306c38c8455f7508213fd5f5e4cf1eb3efb.png] 

Join O to B where point O is the circum centre of the triangle.

⇒ ∠BOA = 2∠BCA

⇒ 2 × 52° 

⇒ 104° 

In ΔBOA

⇒ OB = OA [radius of the circle]

⇒ ∠OBA = ∠OAB

⇒ ∠AOB + ∠OAB + ∠OBA = 180° 

⇒ 2∠OAB = (180° – 104°)

⇒ 2∠OAB = 76° 

⇒ ∠OAB = (76/2)

⇒ ∠OAB = 38° 

In ΔABD

⇒ ∠ABD + ∠BDA + ∠DAB = 180°

Now,

∠DAP = ∠BAO – ∠BAD

questions.question: AB is the diameter of a circle with centre O. C and D are two points on the circumference of the circle on either side of AB, such that ∠CAB = 42° and ∠ABD = 57°. What is difference (in degrees) between the measures of ∠CAD and ∠CBD?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AB is the diameter of a circle with centre O

∠CAB = 42° and ∠ABD = 57°

**Concept used:**

The diameter of a circle makes an angle of 90 degree on the circumference

The opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary which means that the sum of either pair of opposite angles is equal to 180 degrees.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e5204045f62ef5d470a1c548a80de254ab32d503de824e4d34ce5b384873e37.png] 

∠ACB = 90° [∵ AB is diameter]

So, in ΔACB

∠CBA = 180° - ∠ACB - ∠CAB

⇒ ∠CBA = 180° - 90° - 42°

⇒ ∠CBA = 48°

So,

∠CBD = ∠CBA + ∠ABD

⇒ ∠CBD = 48° + 57°

⇒ ∠CBD = 105°

Again,

ADBC is a cyclic qudrialteral 

So, ∠CAD = 180° - ∠CBD

⇒ ∠CAD = 180° - 105°

∠CAD = 75°

Difference = 105° - 75°

⇒ 30°

**∴ The difference (in degrees) between the measures of ∠CAD and ∠CBD is 30°**

questions.question: ΔABC is drawn in a circle such that AC = BC and ∠BAC = 65°. From points B and C two tangents are drawn which intersect at point P. What is the measure of ∠BPC?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

By the Alternate Segment Theorem, the angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle subtended by that chord in the alternate segment.

⇒ ∠PBC = ∠BAC = 65°

⇒ ∠PCB = ∠BAC = 65°

In ΔBPC, the sum of all interior angles is 180°:

⇒ ∠BPC + 65° + 65° = 180°

⇒ ∠BPC = 180° − 130° = 50°

**∴ The correct answer is 50°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ΔABC is inscribed in a circle with center O.

AC = BC and ∠BAC = 65°.

Tangents at B and C meet at external point P.

**Calculations:**

⇒ The angle subtended by chord BC at the circumference is ∠BAC = 65°.

⇒ The angle subtended by an arc at the center is exactly double the angle subtended at the circumference.

⇒ Central Angle ∠BOC = 2 × ∠BAC = 2 × 65° = 130°.

⇒ The radius drawn to the point of contact is directly perpendicular to the tangent line.

⇒ Therefore, ∠OBP = 90° and ∠OCP = 90°.

⇒ In quadrilateral OBPC, the sum of all internal angles is strictly 360°.

⇒ ∠BOC + ∠OBP + ∠BPC + ∠OCP = 360°

⇒ 130° + 90° + ∠BPC + 90° = 360°

⇒ 310° + ∠BPC = 360°

⇒ ∠BPC = 360° − 310° = 50°

**∴ The correct answer is 50°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Alternate Segment Theorem

The angle between a tangent line and a chord passing through the point of contact is perfectly equal to the angle subtended by that same chord in the alternate segment of the circle.

Angle Between Intersecting Tangents

The angle between two distinct tangents drawn from an external given point to a circle is supplementary to the central angle subtended by the chord connecting their respective points of contact (∠P + ∠O = 180°).

Inscribed Angle Theorem

The angle strictly subtended by an arc at the center is mathematically double the angle subtended by it at any remaining part of the circle's circumference.

questions.question: AB is a chord of a circle with centre O and P is any point on the circle. If ∠APB = 122°, then what is the measure of ∠OAB ?

Concept used:

Sum of opposite sides of a cyclic quadrilateral are 180°

The angle subtended by an arc of a circle at its center is twice the angle it subtends anywhere on the circle’s circumference.

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e99344c905022284275a4d1853992192a36e5338ef736ea9d5de7f014e627d3.png]

∠ATB + ∠APB = 180° [sum of opposite angles are 180°]

⇒ x = (180° – 122°)

⇒ x = 58° 

∠ATB = 58° 

And we know that the angle subtended by an arc of a circle at its center is twice the angle it subtends anywhere on the circle’s circumference.

⇒ ∠AOB = 2 × ∠ATB

⇒ ∠AOB = 2 × 58° 

⇒ ∠AOB = 116° 

Now,

OA = OB [radius of the circle]

Then,

∠OAB + ∠AOB + ∠OBA = 180° 

⇒ θ + 116° + θ = 180° 

⇒ 2θ + 116° = 180° 

⇒ 2θ = (180° – 116°)

⇒ 2θ = 64° 

⇒ θ = 32° 

so,

∠OAB = θ = 32° 

∴ The required value of ∠OAB is 32°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e99344c905022284275a4d1853992192a36e5338ef736ea9d5de7f014e627d3.png]

questions.question: Two circles have radii of 27 cm and 36 cm. The distance between their centres is 45 cm. What is the length (in cm) of their common chord?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two circles have radii of 27 cm and 36 cm. The distance between their centres is 45 cm.

**Formula used:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6008f37fd7b12402914c8a9d494de1501df6065c15024a36901891c01373a2bd.png] 

Length of common chord AM = sqrt{(4r₁²d² - (r₁² - r₂² + d²)²) / (4d²)}

Where,

AQ = r₁ = 27 cm

AP = r₂ = 36 cm

PQ = d = 45 cm

**Calculations:**

AM = sqrt{(4 × 27² × 45² - (27² - 36² + 45²)²) / (4 × 45²)}

⇒ AM = sqrt{(4 × 729 × 2025 - (729 - 1296 + 2025)²) / (4 × 2025)}

⇒ AM = sqrt{(5904900 - (1458)²) / 8100}

⇒ AM = sqrt{(5904900 - 2125764) / 8100}

⇒ AM = sqrt{3779136 / 8100}

⇒ AM = sqrt{466.56} = 21.6 cm

⇒ AB = 2 × AM = 2 × 21.6 = 43.2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The radii of the two circles are AQ = 27 cm and AP = 36 cm. The distance between their centers, PQ = 45 cm.

**Concept Used:**

The line joining the centers of the two circles is the perpendicular bisector of the common chord.

Let the length of the common chord be 2x, and let M be the point where the perpendicular bisector intersects the chord. The distances from the centers of the circles to the chord will form right-angled triangles.

**Calculation:**

Let the distance between the centers of the two circles be PQ = 45 cm.

Let the radius of the first circle be AQ = 27 cm, and the radius of the second circle be AP = 36 cm.

We need to find the distance AM (which is half the length of the common chord).

From the Pythagorean theorem, in triangle AQM (where A is the center of the first circle), we have:

AQ² = AM² + QM²

27² = AM² + QM²

729 = AM² + QM²

AM² = 729 - QM² ----(1)

Similarly, in triangle APM (where A is the center of the second circle), we have:

AP² = AM² + PM²

36² = AM² + PM²

1296 = AM² + PM²

Rearranging, we get:

Now expand and simplify the equation:

729 - QM² = 1296 - (2025 - 90QM + QM²)

729 - QM² = 1296 - 2025 + 90QM - QM²

questions.question: If two circles of radii 35 cm and 25 cm touch each other externally, then the length (in cm) of a common tangent is (Rounded off to 2 decimal places)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the first circle (R₁) = 35 cm

Radius of the second circle (R₂) = 25 cm

**Formula Used:**

Length of the common external tangent = √{d² - (R1 - R2)²}

**Calculation:**

Distance between the centers of the circles (d) = R₁ + R₂

d = 35 + 25

d = 60 cm

Length of the common external tangent = √{d² - (R1 - R2)²}

√{60² - (35 - 25)²}

√{60² - 10²}

√{3600 - 100}

√3500 ≈ 59.16

Length of the common external tangent = 59.16 cm

**The length of the common tangent is 59.16 cm.**
